sentences.text: Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned Senior Advocates for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are arrayed as accused Nos.2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10.
They are innocent and law abiding citizens.
They have not committed any offence as alleged.
They have been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
Petitioners are the Directors and Employees of the Bonito Designs Private Limited, which is an interior designing company.
There was an agreement entered into between the Company and the complainant to carry out the interior designing of her house and the Company agreed to carryout the interiors for a specific amount.
Accordingly, Company had carried more than 50% of the work as per the directions of the complainant, even though the designs were changed.
The complainant paid an amount of Rs.11,72,272/-.
There were frequent exchange of e-mail and finally on 17.08.2022, the complainant sent an e-mail stating that she does not want to continue the project with the Company.
Later during December, 2022, the police complaint was filed stating that the price quoted by the Company was much higher and thereby Company has committed the offence.
Learned Senior Advocates submitted that it is purely a civil dispute between the parties.
But in spite of that, false allegations are made giving the colour of the criminal case.
The Investigating Officer without authority, ordered for freezing the Bank Account of the Company.
However, a writ petition was filed before this Court, wherein, the account was defreezed with a lien on specified amount, which is said to be due to the complainant.
4. Learned Senior Advocates further submitted that since the petitioners are Directors and Employees of the Company in question, they are not required for custodial interrogation.
They are very much available for investigation.
There is reasonable apprehension of being arrested.

Hence,
they are before this Court.
They are the permanent residents of the addresses mentioned in the cause-title to the petitions and they are ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, they pray to allow the petitions in the interest of justice.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petitions submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioners for having committed the offence.
The informant lodged the first information making specific allegations against the Company.
The petitioners have not appeared before the Investigating Officer till today.
They are absconding since from the date of registration of the case.
If they are granted anticipatory bail, they may never turn up before the Investigating Officer and they may abscond or may commit similar offences, threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
Therefore, the petitioners are not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petitions.

6. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:

sentences.text: The informant made it clear that there was an agreement entered into between her sister and the Company in question.
The petitioners are said to be the Directors and Employees of Company.

Several correspondences are produced before this Court and the last one is dated 17.08.2022, said to have been sent by the complainant stating that she does not want to continue the Project with the Company and thereafter, this first information was came to be filed.

The order of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, passed in W.P.No.10/2023 discloses that the freezing of the Account was lifted by keeping the lien for an amount of Rs.11,72,272/- which was paid by the sister of the informant.
Admittedly, the dispute has arisen out of the agreement entered into between the parties on 20.05.2022.
Under such circumstances, I do not find any reason to reject the claim of the petitioners for pre-arrest bail.

Hence, I am - 10 - of the opinion that the petitioners may be granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the apprehensions expressed by the learned High Court Government Pleader that the petitioners may abscond or may tamper or threaten the prosecution witnesses.

8. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petitions are allowed.
The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.334/2022 of H.S.R.Layout Police Station, Bengaluru.

The petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.
The petitioners shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
